Q6_check_content_access_retention.decision: DIVERGE from conformance section F5. PR-07 retains all 30 check_content_access call sites instead of substituting them for Viewer.
Q6_check_content_access_retention.rationale: Migration 062 adds `visibility varchar(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'public'` to every tier_a table and backfills nothing. No PR before PR-12 transcribes ownership.partition_type into claims.visibility. So TODAY every spliced viewer predicate matches every row, and check_content_access is the only control with live effect on the handlers that have one. Deleting the sites now would take a fixture-private claim from redacted to fully readable by a stranger's token - the removal, not the retention, would be the fail-open. Two filters compose strictly narrower than either.

Justified by CLAUDE.md ('All SQL stays in crates/epigraph-db/src/repos/'): the {VISIBILITY:...} marker convention is a repo-layer convention and a handler cannot splice a predicate into SQL it does not own.

Same exfiltration primitive ClaimRepository::rag_hybrid_context documents as 'the single highest-value exfiltration primitive in the API'. Fixed in rag.rs in the first pass and missed here because the self-audit was scoped to touched files. Now ClaimRepository::semantic_search_flat + semantic_graph_neighbors.
scope_substitution.graph_query_utils.rs_load_subgraph: Shared helper reached from 3 handlers, took no Viewer, projected claims.content into every node label. Now takes &Viewer; claims/evidence/edges all filtered via GraphViewRepository::subgraph_*.
scope_substitution.assess.rs_assess_claim: Held a Viewer and loaded its subject claim with a bare keyed read - an existence-and-content oracle, and the reason an authenticated stranger could attach evidence to another tenant's claim. Now ClaimRepository::get_by_id.
scope_substitution.membership_table_filters: claim_cluster_membership and claim_neighborhood_membership ARE in migration 062's tier_a array. All 4 join sites in graph_view.rs now splice /* {VISIBILITY:m} */. The module doc previously discussed only the non-tenancy-bearing graph_* metadata tables and was silent on these two.
scope_substitution.node_edge_consistency: graph_neighborhood.rs's node projections became viewer-filtered while its 4 edge projections did not, so responses could name ids absent from `nodes` - an id-enumeration oracle. Edges and compound_groups.member_atom_ids are now constrained to the surviving node set.
scope_substitution.version_history_correctness: ORDER BY depth is not a total order and superseded_by was derived from row POSITION, which is wrong at a fork (mark_duplicate points every duplicate at the same canonical claim). Now ORDER BY depth, id with superseded_by read from claims.supersedes, plus a depth-100 cap on both recursive terms (a supersession cycle A->B->A is accepted by mark_duplicate's guard and previously spun a backend forever; the request pool sets no statement_timeout).
scope_substitution.graph.rs_expand_truncated: `truncated` was `total_size > nodes.len()` where total_size is unfiltered graph_clusters.size and nodes is now filtered - it reported true for a complete response and its difference was an exact count of hidden claims. Now derived from the budget.

open_findings.what: `None => return ContentAccess::Full, // No ownership -> public` is FAIL-OPEN
open_findings.detail: Any claim with no `ownership` row returns FULL content to any authenticated caller. Ownership rows are written only by explicit assignment, so for the majority of the corpus this backward-compat branch makes the whole check_content_access pass a no-op. This is why several PR-07 findings are 'live today for un-owned claims' rather than purely latent.
open_findings.assigned: PR-12 (the backfill that gives every claim an ownership/tenancy row is what makes the branch unreachable), removal in PR-14
